paper.title: EvolveRouter: Co-Evolving Routing and Prompt for Multi-Agent Question Answering
paper.central_claim: EvolveRouter couples graph-based per-query routing with targeted agent-instruction refinement in a closed-loop co-evolution process (router diagnostics guide prompt rewrites; refined agents give cleaner router supervision) and adds an adaptive inference rule that sets collaboration size per query via router-weighted answer agreement; it consistently outperforms SOTA routing baselines in F1 and EM on five QA benchmarks.
paper.claim_scope: Five QA benchmarks (2Wiki, HotpotQA, NewsQA, TriviaQA, NGQA; plus GLEN-Bench in appendix), 24-agent pool (4 backbones x 6 roles), per-benchmark training with 500/100/100 train/val/test items, 3 seeds.

evidence.quote: Motivating observation: agent quality is highly context-dependent, and no single agent configuration is consistently optimal.
evidence.support_explanation: Heterogeneity of agents across task/backbone/prompt is the stated premise for differentiated treatment.

evidence.quote: most prior routing methods treat agent behavior as fixed, optimizing only
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: routers do not improve the agents they route to.

evidence.quote: We collect four types of diagnostic signals during training: agent-level performance summaries per backbone–role pair, a failure archive of incorrect examples with gold answers and router weights, router weight statistics indicating which agents are most relied upon, and a prompt-aware answer cache that automatically invalidates entries when prompts change.
evidence.support_explanation: Information visible to the prompt improver: failure archive with gold answers and router weights; cache keyed on prompts.

evidence.quote: A role becomes eligible for prompt refinement only if it underperforms on multiple backbones.
evidence.support_explanation: Role-level consistency filter separating prompt-level weakness from backbone-specific outliers (partition by discriminating property).

evidence.quote: This rule prioritizes agents that perform poorly but still receive high routing weight.
evidence.support_explanation: Priority = severity x (alpha + mean router weight); router reliance is the discriminator for which agent to treat.

evidence.quote: Rewriting is constrained to preserve the role’s core reasoning strategy and output format, and may only add, rephrase, or remove a small number of sentences.
evidence.support_explanation: Bounded, localized edit operator on the instruction text.

evidence.quote: A candidate is accepted only if it does not cause significant regression on the targeted validation subset and yields a non-negative net improvement at the sample level.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated acceptance rule for retaining a rewritten prompt.

evidence.quote: The acceptance rule used in code is more permissive than a strict “new mean must be larger than old mean” criterion.
evidence.support_explanation: The implemented gate tolerates small mean drops (delta) if sample-level improvements offset; text rule and code rule differ and delta is not given.

evidence.quote: After fine-tuning, we apply a validation-based safety check and revert the update if the new router causes regression.
evidence.support_explanation: Rollback exists for the router; no analogous rollback for already-accepted prompts is described.

evidence.locator: Appendix B.1 Target budget and freezing
evidence.quote: Agents that experience repeated failed rewrite attempts are frozen and removed from future rounds.
evidence.support_explanation: Freeze rule after 3 consecutive rejections (k_freeze=3 given in same paragraph).

evidence.quote: cumulative gains reaching +1.31% F1 on 2Wiki, +3.75% on HotpotQA, +9.21% on TriviaQA, and +6.67% on NGQA
evidence.support_explanation: Reported relative F1 gains of PO over the router-only base (test splits).

evidence.locator: Sec.4.4 The worst agent is not the most valuable to fix
evidence.quote: However, Table 4 shows that this strategy yields marginal gains on 2Wiki and HotpotQA, slightly hurts NewsQA, and barely changes NGQA.
evidence.support_explanation: Diagnostic-guided target selection is compared with a lowest-F1 heuristic.

evidence.locator: Sec.4.4 Routing knowledge must be preserved
evidence.quote: Retraining the router from scratch after prompt optimization consistently underperforms checkpoint resuming, with F1 gaps of +0.75 on 2Wiki, +1.88 on HotpotQA, +0.92 on NewsQA, and +4.92 on NGQA
evidence.support_explanation: Router-retraining ablation (resume vs scratch).

evidence.quote: From each benchmark we sample 500 training, 100 validation, and 100 test instances.
evidence.support_explanation: Split sizes: held-out test is only 100 instances per benchmark.

evidence.quote: are tuned on the validation split for each dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Adaptive-K thresholds (tau, k_min, k_max) tuned on validation, not test.

evidence.quote: At inference time, Adaptive K reduces the average number of agent calls from 24 to 2.9–7.4 across our benchmarks, yielding a 69–88% reduction while maintaining or improving F1.
evidence.support_explanation: Inference-call accounting for Adaptive K.

evidence.quote: Each refinement round modifies only 2–3 agents, keeping the incremental cost at roughly 10% of the full evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Training-side cost statement (calls, not tokens/dollars); rewriter and candidate-validation cost not itemized.

evidence.quote: The results reveal that cross-dataset routing consistently underperforms in-domain training by a wide margin.
evidence.support_explanation: Counter-evidence on generality: router (and PO) are per-benchmark.

evidence.quote: EvolveRouter consistently achieves the strongest performance among all practical baselines, improving over the best structure-aware routing baseline on every dataset in both F1 and EM.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline comparison claim.

evidence.quote: EvolveRouter is the first framework to jointly support routing, prompt optimization, and training in a multi-agent setting.
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty claim made by a feature-table, not by empirical comparison.
Full-system test results (2Wiki F1/EM; NewsQA F1/EM; NGQA F1/EM shown in this row).
Router-only baseline (numerically identical to the AgentRouter row of Table 3).
Worst-only target selection falls below the base on NewsQA and TriviaQA F1.

evidence.quote: Adaptive K exceeds the best fixed-K setting on every dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Adaptive K vs fixed K ablation claim.

evidence.quote: Best Agent selects the single strongest backbone–role pair per dataset, representing the best achievable performance without any collaboration.
evidence.support_explanation: Best Agent is chosen per dataset; the selection split is not stated.

evidence.quote: We use GPT-4o-mini as the rewriter LLM.
evidence.support_explanation: Rewriter LLM is an extra model call source not matched in baselines.

evidence.quote: attributes each agent’s contribution through approximate Shapley values and rewrites underperforming prompts online.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest adjacent: HiveMind already rewrites underperforming agent prompts in multi-agent settings.

evidence.quote: shows that prompt optimization and topology optimization are interdependent through alternating optimization.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest adjacent: MASS (alternating prompt/topology optimization).

evidence.quote: Prior work optimizes prompts either for individual agents or within a fixed multi-agent structure.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-claimed differentiation from multi-agent prompt-optimization lines.

evidence.quote: average all results over three seeds
evidence.support_explanation: Seed count for all reported means/stds.

evidence.support_explanation: Rounds are capped by plateau; stopping decided by validation (not stated explicitly).

signatures.object: Per-agent role prompts (instruction text) of 24 backbone-role agents in a fixed agent pool (non-weight, prompt artifact).
signatures.information: Failure archive of incorrect training examples with gold answers and router weights, per-agent F1 summaries, router weight statistics; gold-label F1 on the 500 training items; validation subset centered on diagnosed failures plus extra validation samples. Test items not visible.
signatures.operation: Rank backbone-role pairs by priority = (1-meanF1)(alpha+mean router weight) after a role-level cross-backbone consistency filter; for top N_max=3 pairs a GPT-4o-mini rewriter makes 3 candidate rewrites (temps 0.30/0.45/0.60) adding/rephrasing/removing 1-3 sentences.
signatures.output: Accepted rewritten prompt replaces the incumbent prompt for that agent; otherwise unchanged; frozen after 3 consecutive rejections.
signatures.conditions: Role must underperform on >=tau_bb backbones (3, relaxed to 2 then 1 if none); role strategy and output format must be preserved.
signatures.feedback: F1 against gold on training/validation items; router weights as reliance signal.
signatures.selection_rule: Best candidate on targeted validation subset; accept if mean F1 >= old - delta AND at least one sample improves AND NOT(mean lower AND more degradations than improvements) (code rule; Sec.3.2 text states no significant regression and non-negative net sample-level improvement). delta value not given.
signatures.selection_data: Targeted validation subset (diagnosed failures + supplemental validation samples); router regression check on validation F1 (revert if >0.03 drop).
signatures.persistence: Accepted prompts are kept in the agent pool across rounds (max ~3); answer cache keyed on prompt hash invalidates only changed agents; router checkpoint chained across rounds.
signatures.later_use: Re-queried refined agents produce new soft F1 targets used to fine-tune the router (resumed checkpoint); refined prompts are the ones used for test-time agent calls and voting.
signatures.claimed_effect: Relative F1 gains of PO over router-only base: 1.31% (2Wiki), 3.75% (HotpotQA), 2.32% (NewsQA), 9.21% (TriviaQA), 6.67% (NGQA).
signatures.failure_boundary: Routing and PO do not transfer across benchmarks (Table 8); per-benchmark training required; worst-only target selection hurts on NewsQA/TriviaQA.

signatures.object: Inference-time collaboration size K(q) (number of agents consulted per query); not retained state.
signatures.information: Router-ranked agent list for the query; answers of consulted agents; router weights.
signatures.operation: Query agents sequentially in router order; stop when router-weighted agreement of the top answer >= tau after k_min agents (k<=k_max).
signatures.conditions: tau, k_min, k_max tuned on the validation split of each dataset.
signatures.feedback: None at inference (agreement among agents only).
signatures.persistence: not_applicable: per-query computation; only the tuned thresholds persist.
signatures.claimed_effect: Calls reduced from 24 to 2.9-7.4 (69-88%) with maintained or improved F1; beats best fixed K on every dataset.
signatures.failure_boundary: Gains over base router are small (+0.7 to +1.5 F1 relative); agreement signal depends on PO-improved agents.

signatures.object: RouterGNN weights (heterogeneous GNN over query-entity-agent graph) - weight-trained B-side component of the loop.
signatures.information: Soft targets from per-agent token-F1 against gold answers on training items.
signatures.operation: KL training to softmax(F1/tau) targets; later rounds fine-tune from previous checkpoint after prompt updates.
signatures.output: Per-query agent distribution used for ranking, weighting and priority scoring.
signatures.conditions: Reverted if validation F1 drops by more than 0.03.
signatures.persistence: Checkpoint chain across rounds (weights, outside non-weight scope; evaluated here only as a loop component).
signatures.later_use: Defines which agents are consulted and how heavily they are weighted.
signatures.claimed_effect: Resume-from-checkpoint beats retraining from scratch by +0.75 to +4.92 F1.

gap.author_gap: Routing methods optimize which agent to invoke but treat agent behavior (prompts) as fixed, and rely on rigid participation schemes (single agent or a fixed pool).
gap.checked_gap: The fixed-pool premise holds for the cited routers (GraphRouter, AgentRouter, RouteLLM, etc.), but multi-agent prompt optimizers that rewrite underperforming agents (HiveMind, MAPRO) and alternating prompt/topology optimization (MASS) already exist and appear in Table 2 yet are not experimental baselines. The checked residue is narrower: using router-induced reliance (severity x router weight) to choose which agent prompt to refine and re-training the router on the refined pool.
gap.lineage: AgentRouter (heterogeneous-GNN KG router with soft-F1 supervision; the paper reuses it as the "KG Router (base)" - Table 3 and Table 4 rows are numerically identical) -> + closed-loop prompt refinement with gated acceptance -> + answer-agreement adaptive K. Prompt-refinement ancestors: GRACE (gated refinement with rejection control, single-agent), HiveMind, MAPRO, MASS.
closest_adjacent: HiveMind: Shapley-style per-agent contribution then online prompt rewrite (E27)
MASS: alternating prompt and topology optimization (E28)
MAPRO: MAP-inference prompt optimization over agent DAG (named in related work)
GRACE: gated prompt refinement with rejection control (single agent)
gap.residue: Agents with low F1 but high router weight carry disproportionate error; refinement targeted by F1 alone (worst-only) is shown to be inferior on NewsQA/TriviaQA.
gap.stakes: Per-benchmark F1 gains of ~1-6 points (relative 1.3%-9.2%) and 69-88% fewer agent calls at inference.
gap.method_response: Router diagnostics (failure archive + router weights) pick targets; a gated rewrite loop edits prompts; router is fine-tuned on refined agents; agreement-based K trims calls.
gap.remaining_gap: No head-to-head with HiveMind/MASS/MAPRO or generic prompt optimizers under equal budget; no gate-off/random-rewrite control; routing and PO do not transfer; only 100 test items per benchmark.
unresolved: Whether gains exceed those of generic multi-agent prompt optimizers at equal rewriter/validation budget.
Whether the benefit comes from prompt content or from the additional router fine-tuning epochs per round.

matches.reason: The operation actually performed is partitioning a heterogeneous resource (24 agents) by a measured property and applying differentiated treatment (selective prompt refinement, per-query K). C04 (compression of over-provisioned trained artifacts) does not describe this operation, so sub_id is null. Fit is partial because the card family is built around model/parameter heterogeneity.

rs_pattern.reason: Best-fit original main card selected on the executed operation (differentiated treatment of a heterogeneous agent pool); sub-card null because the only child C04 covers compression of trained artifacts.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial - differentiated treatment beats uniform/worst-only treatment in the paper own ablation, but no uniform or random-target baseline is reported.

matches.reason: A single textual artifact class (agent instruction prompts) is rewritten from diagnosed failures, scored on a validation subset and retained only if it passes a regression-tolerant gate; edits are small and bounded.

unassigned: Router-weight-conditioned target selection (severity weighted by downstream reliance) has no counterpart condition in the H10/attribute_and_patch cards.
Adaptive-K answer-agreement stopping is an inference-time rule outside the retention pattern set.

revision_proposals.text: Consider a condition covering consumer-reliance-weighted target selection (fix the artifact the downstream consumer relies on most), single-source evidence.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Partition of the agent pool into prompt-level-weak vs backbone-outlier roles and by reliance-weighted severity (RS: partition by discriminating property) maps to choosing which prompt document to attribute failures to and patch (domain: attribute then localized edit).
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS card concerns heterogeneity of components inside one model/resource and requires a partition criterion shown load-bearing; domain H10 requires critique-driven rewrite plus regression-checked retention. Overlap is the selection of what to edit; the domain card does not need the heterogeneity partition and the RS card does not cover retention gating.

expectations.reason: Fig.1 and Tables 5-6 show per-agent F1 varies by task, backbone and prompt.

expectations.question: Is every component of the treatment justified by an ablation isolating its contribution?
expectations.reason: PO and Adaptive K are ablated separately and worst-only/scratch variants exist, but the role-consistency filter, multi-candidate sampling, validation gate and freeze rule are not individually ablated.

expectations.applies_when: Gain is attributed to the decomposition rather than added capacity.

expectations.question: Is efficiency measured in deployment units (latency/tokens/dollars)?

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Prompt refinement driven by router-reliance-weighted failure diagnostics, with a regression-tolerant validation gate and a resumed router, improves in-distribution held-out F1/EM (n=100 per benchmark, 3 seeds) over the same router without refinement, and Adaptive K cuts agent calls by 69-88% with similar or better F1.
not_supported: Superiority over other multi-agent prompt optimizers (not compared).
That the validation gate or the target-selection formula individually causes the gain beyond the worst-only comparison.
Cross-task transfer of routers or refined prompts (contradicted by Table 8 for routers, partial for prompts).
unresolved: Cost in tokens/dollars of rewriter and candidate validation.
Chosen-round decision rule for reported per-round numbers.
assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; no run by this reviewer (no our_run evidence).

G.reason: Real limitation (fixed agent pool) with reasonable evidence from Fig.1, and the delta over the immediate parent (AgentRouter) is explicit. But nearest neighbors that already optimize multi-agent prompts (HiveMind, MAPRO, MASS) are only contrasted verbally; the first-framework claim rests on a feature table and the residual (router-reliance-based targeting) is narrower than the stated gap.

M.reason: Operation-to-problem chain is reconstructable: failure archive + router weights -> priority -> bounded rewrite -> gated acceptance -> cache-based re-query -> resumed router. The reasoning for reliance-weighted targeting is argued and tested against worst-only; resume-vs-scratch has a mechanistic explanation. Distinguishing predictions against uniform/random targeting and ungated rewriting are not tested, so not 4.

X.reason: Selection, acceptance, freeze, router revert, cache invalidation and chained checkpoints are all specified with parameters (N_max=3, 3 candidates, temperatures, freeze=3, 0.03 revert). Weaknesses: delta is unspecified, the text and code gates differ, there is no rollback of accepted prompts, no version history of prompts, and no staleness handling.

E.measurement.reason: Standard token-F1 and EM against gold answers on established QA benchmarks, mean and std over 3 seeds; no LLM judge. Concerns: tiny 100-item test sets, NGQA EM near 10% for the best system, and the Best Agent baseline is chosen per dataset without stating the split.

E.causality.reason: Useful ablations: PO vs Adaptive K contribution, worst-only target selection, router resume vs scratch, rounds. Missing: ungated/random rewrite control, equal-budget prompt-optimizer baselines, control for additional router fine-tuning epochs and extra LLM calls given only to the PO arm; baselines get no prompt optimization.

E.holdout.reason: Separate 100-item test split per benchmark and thresholds tuned on validation, so selection and test are separated. Only in-distribution, per-benchmark; routing/prompt transfer is poor (Table 8); no contamination analysis for public benchmarks and models; rewriter sees training failures with gold labels.

E.statistics.reason: 3 seeds with mean+/-std and many datasets; test n=100 gives coarse EM; no confidence intervals or significance tests; several PO gains (e.g. 2Wiki +1 F1) are close to seed std; rejected-candidate and freeze counts are not reported.

E.cost.reason: Inference-call reduction (24 -> 2.9-7.4) and incremental training cost (~10% of full evaluation per round, 12,000 calls for stage 1, GNN minutes) are reported. No token/dollar/latency numbers, rewriter and candidate-validation calls are not itemized, and baselines are not budget-matched.
